card.name: Irish dance
card.era: Traditional; competitive stepdance codified late 19th-20th c.; globalized 1994 (Riverdance)
card.tagline: Umbrella of Irish stepdance, ceili and set dancing.
card.profile: Irish dance is a group of traditional dance forms originating in Ireland, broadly divided into social dances (ceili and set dancing) and performance/solo dances (stepdance) (Wikipedia). Modern competitive stepdance is characterized by a rigid upper body and intricate, fast footwork in soft shoes (ghillies) or hard shoes; other solo forms include sean-nos (relaxed, close-to-the-floor, improvised) and festival dance. Ceili dancing is performed by groups of 2-16 to reels, jigs and hornpipes; the 30 standardized ceili dances appear in CLRG's official handbook 'Ar Rinci Ceili.' Set dances derive from French quadrilles for four couples. Accompaniment is Irish traditional music - fiddle, bodhran, concertina, flute, whistle. The form was globally popularized by Riverdance (1994).
card.insight: Irish group dancing was particularly influenced by the French quadrille in the late 18th century - a genuine France connection, but the tradition is unambiguously Irish, so the catalog's France label is a mislabel (Wikipedia).

parts.note: Welcomes viewers and introduces the beginner Irish dance tutorial series.
Explains foot distinction using a white sock and a black sock for easy following.
Breaks down the first point and switch-foot movement.
Introduces and explains the cut movement.
Teaches the reverse combination starting on the left foot.

steps.name: Point
steps.description: Pointing the big toe forward onto the floor.

steps.name: Switch Point
steps.description: Switching feet to point with the opposite toe.

steps.name: Cut
steps.description: Bringing the foot up and over in a dab-like motion.

cues: Touch the floor with our big toe
images: imagine your leg is doing a dab
common_mistakes: Tripping yourself over when bringing the leg down
lessons.teacher_style: The instructor uses a structured, step-by-step approach with clear verbal explanations and physical demonstrations. He breaks down movements using descriptive metaphors and helpful visual aids like contrasting socks.
lessons.distinctive_method: Using mismatched colored socks (one white, one black) to teach left and right foot coordination.
what_works: Using contrasting white and black socks to clearly identify left and right feet.
Showing both front and back view demonstrations so viewers can mirror easily.
what_hinders: Some explanations get slightly conversational and off-topic.
